correctness.rationale: Exact Gaussian conditional quadratic projection gives risk 1/3 minus twice the sum of squared selected Gram entries. Independently integrating shifted-Legendre antiderivatives verifies the sparse Gram structure, with a single 0–1 edge and decreasing parity edges. Strict parity-prefix compression and strictly decreasing marginal scores prove global uniqueness for all budgets; an explicit partial-fraction telescoping identity proves the rational all-m error. Spectral min-max for the Volterra covariance proves best unrestricted linear sensing and the sharp ratio. Standalone rational tests verified the small Gram block, all subsets of the first 13 modes through size 7, and the risk identity through m=100. Finite checking is not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The asserted distinct theorem is universal optimality of the first m Legendre white-noise coordinates among all m-mode subsets for Brownian quadratic path-energy Bayes risk and its exact all-budget ratio against optimal unrestricted Gaussian linear sensing. Foster–Lyons–Oberhauser already prove the first-two-coordinate conditional formula; it is excluded from the novelty claim. Kuznetsov supplies broad Fourier error formulas, but not this allocation/efficiency theorem. published-finding corpus mathematical statements retrieved concerned different Brownian and mode-selection objectives; no checked statement entails the claim. Older equivalent results are a residual priority risk. Grebenkov’s Gaussian-quadratic-statistic optimization chooses the statistic itself, not an observation subspace for a fixed payoff.
residual_risks: General Gaussian quadratic-functional observation design or classical orthogonal polynomial projection theory may contain an equivalent all-index-set optimization that was not indexed by searched terms.
Kuznetsov’s broad Fourier MSE formula subsumes parts of the coefficient calculations; the new allocation-and-efficiency theorem must not be credited to those routine calculations.
Two-coefficient conditional energy results from 2019 are prior art; no novelty is attributed to that case.
Published-result summaries are not full-text source inspections; this is insufficient to rule out all unindexed equivalents.

value.rationale: Choosing m polynomial Wiener coordinates to simulate under a finite Gaussian budget is a natural stochastic numerical approximation problem, and quadratic integrated Brownian energy is a nonlinear positive path observable. The all-m unique mode allocation and exact performance penalty relative to unrestricted Gaussian linear measurements are motivated design-level facts, not a fixed low-order calculation or a mere substitution. The known m=2 identity and basic Fourier error method are explicitly excluded from the distinct contribution.
